Thanks for flagging — I pulled the rollout logs and kernel-selection traces. No code push occurred in serving; we did flip a new compilation profile for model-12f at 07:38 PT to optimize memory on the new weights. That profile changes kernel ordering and KV-cache prefetch behavior; it looks like, for a subset of sequence shapes that ClearBridge uses (long prompt + multi-turn), the prefetch path increased stall time.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Option A (fastest, lowest risk to accuracy): traffic shift to previous variant (model-12f-stable) for ClearBridge account only. This is a pure routing rollback and should drop p95 back to baseline.
- Option B (runtime patch): revert the compilation profile globally for model-12f (requires ~20m to stage and validate) — lower blast radius than a full rollback but affects all customers on model-12f during staging.
- Option C (fallback): enable quantized-lite fallback variant (model-12f-q4-lite) for ClearBridge only — very fast to enable (~5m) but note ~1–1.5% delta in top-k similarity on edge cases (we'll provide evals).

Attached is a short runbook: runbook_quantized-fallback.md. My recommendation: implement Option A for an immediate 30-minute mitigation window while we validate and run targeted perf traces. We'll then either re-enable model-12f with the prefetch fix or keep ClearBridge on the stable variant until the next safe deployment.

Kim
Kimberly Park
